reviewer: Claude (independent, read-only source review; host scratch tests only)
subject: J293/T8103 bounded CDC proxy window in sources/m1n1-boot-window (base 121fcbf35d4501814b58ca5347926a4173b6a512)

scope.host_scratch_tests: Compiled integrations/m1-boot-window/test_window.c plus a reviewer adversarial test against the candidate's m1_boot_window.c in the reviewer scratchpad; both passed.

contract_checks.requirement: No host, partial frame or bad NOP can block Linux
contract_checks.evidence: uartproxy_wait_m1_boot_window: monotonic get_ticks deadline checked before every byte read and in the outer loop; reads only after iodev_can_read>0, one byte at a time, a 256-byte budget per port per pass, and mdelay(1) between passes. Expiry returns false, main.c prints and falls through to the unchanged payload path. With a valid trailer, stage1_proxy_payload_action returns NATIVE before consulting any USB state (src/stage1_proxy.c:37-38).

contract_checks.requirement: Only a fully checksum-validated NOP claims
contract_checks.evidence: valid_nop requires ff 55 aa 00 (REQ_NOP) and the m1n1 wire checksum (init 0xDEADBEEF, x31337 + (b^0x5A) over 60 bytes, ^0xADDEDBAD), identical to uartproxy.c:222-256, using a per-port rolling 64-byte window. Scratch tests: valid REQ_PROXY, a single bit flip and a NOP split across ports never claim; noise followed by a valid NOP claims on the correct port.

m1_boot_window_feed applies expiry before accepting any byte, so expiry wins even on the final byte of a valid NOP, and TIMEOUT is sticky (scratch-tested). Note: usb_init/usb_iodev_init run before the window clock starts, so total added boot time is USB bring-up plus 10 s.

contract_checks.requirement: Normal NOP dispatcher, reply and feature state unchanged
contract_checks.evidence: The claimed 64 bytes are copied into UartRequest from .type (layout _pad,type,union,checksum); uartproxy_run uses them once on window_iodev, re-verifies the checksum and dispatches normally; later iterations use the unchanged sync path. Exception-mode (start != NULL) behavior is unchanged.

The window sets run_actions' local usb_up before usb_init/usb_iodev_init, so the later fallback guard skips re-init (main.c:245). uartproxy_wait_stage1 initializes USB itself, but stage1_config_window_ms returns 0 unless J613_ESP_STAGE1 || (CHAINLOADING && !ESP_STAGE2) (stage1_config.c:12), and the Makefile forces ESP_STAGE2=1 for M1_BOOT_WINDOW. main.c rejects EARLY_PROXY_TIMEOUT, USE_DEBUG_USB and BRINGUP.
No stubbed results; a claim enters the real proxy, and after acquisition Linux fallthrough is deliberately forbidden until a next stage is set.

m1_boot_window_allowed requires chip_id 0x8103, ADT target-type exactly J293 with length 5, and a non-debug build; otherwise no USB init and no window. Scratch-tested against J313, T8112, debug, NULL, wrong length and extra characters. The code is compiled only with M1_BOOT_WINDOW=1 plus ESP_STAGE2=1.

findings.finding: Every J293 boot now runs usb_init, whose usb_init_one calls tps6598x_powerup and tps6598x_disable_irqs: all port-controller interrupt flags are acknowledged and INT_MASK1 is written to zero (src/usb.c:310-321, src/tps6598x.c:243-253). The saved masks are restored only by usb_hpm_restore_irqs, called from P_VECTOR (src/proxy.c:110) and HV init (src/hv/hv.c:175). The native Linux-trailer handoff tears down dwc3 (usb_iodev_shutdown, main.c:361-364) but never restores the masks. Before this candidate, a normal J293 stage-2 boot did not run usb_init, so Linux inherited untouched masks.
findings.impact: Linux boots, but its Type-C controller may start with all event interrupts masked unless the Linux tipd/cd321x driver rewrites INT_MASK1 at probe (not verified here). Possible effect: missed USB-C or PD events on the DFU port that also carries VDM serial.
fix_options: On window expiry, before falling through, call usb_hpm_restore_irqs(true), mirroring P_VECTOR.
Or show on hardware that Linux reprograms the masks: compare tipd probe logs and interrupt counts after a window-expired boot against the baseline image.

findings.finding: A successful claim deliberately prevents Linux fallthrough (main.c loops on uartproxy_run until next_stage.entry). If the host dies after claiming, the target stays in the proxy until an external reset. That is acceptable only because the S1 halt-and-VDM reset path is qualified; after a reset the window expires without a host and Linux boots.

The window adds USB bring-up plus 10 s to every J293 boot; adjust the unattended return budgets (cycle 1 returned in about 25 s on the previous image). The custom build tag will not match host_console.py's pinned TAG check, which fails closed; the packet and receipt tooling must name this image explicitly.

W1_follow_up.source_fix: main.c records window_timed_out only on window expiry. In the payload_action == STAGE1_PAYLOAD_NATIVE branch it calls usb_hpm_restore_irqs(true) before returning to the unchanged next-stage handoff (usb_cdc_cleanup, usb_iodev_shutdown), mirroring P_VECTOR's restore-then-handoff order. The claimed-window path and the invalid-payload proxy fallback are unchanged.
W1_follow_up.partial_init_guards_verified_in_unmodifi: usb_hpm_restore_irqs_match rejects out-of-range HPM indices and requires tps6598x_irq_state[idx].valid (usb.c:358-371). tps6598x_disable_irqs returns before setting valid if the mask read fails and sets valid before the clear/mask writes (tps6598x.c:235-241), so only a genuinely saved INT_MASK1 is ever restored. force=true only bypasses the port-in-use check, as P_VECTOR does.
W1_follow_up.link_evidence: In linked run_actions, stage1_proxy_payload_action's NATIVE result (cbz w0 to 0x4a1d4) tests the window_timed_out flag (tbz w19), then sets w0=1 and calls usb_hpm_restore_irqs at 0x4a1dc before the 'Valid payload found' debug_printf and return. The window call (uartproxy_wait_m1_boot_window at 0x4a0c4) precedes payload_run (0x4a154). The artifact hashes match the receipt.
remaining_limits: Restore I2C failures are logged but the helper returns void; Linux could still inherit cleared masks on such a failure.
Event flags acknowledged by usb_init are not reconstructed.
Whether Linux tipd/cd321x behaves normally after the restored handoff is hardware-unverified.
First persistent boot needs one-time owner availability with a manual Recovery rollback; no non-persistent launch path exists in the original stage2.

limits: Source review plus host scratch tests only; no ARM build, link or run by the reviewer.

Not verified: USB controller event handling cost, iodev_read non-blocking behavior when can_read>0 on the real dwc3 path, and console write behavior if a host holds the CDC port open without reading (inherited base behavior).
Linux tipd/cd321x mask handling at probe is unknown; W1 needs a fix or hardware evidence.
